page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a woodcut ornament and a chapter heading above the text. No marginal notes. Top: running head "Cap.50." at left and "AVGVSTINVS" at centre. Below the text: catchword at right.

main_text.p: usque pedes involuebant. Quem baptizandi ri-tum retinuerūt imprimis Eunomiani, post Eu-nomij in Pamphylia exilium, quo ab Imperatore Constantino multatus est. Nam hos etiā formam Baptismi postea mutasse, scribit Socrat. lib.5.cap.24.de quibus conqueritur Chrysosto. Homil.1.in Galat. Atque hæc sunt pauca quidē numero, sed veneno & fœtore maxima erroris Arianorum capita, quæ Satan in magnam ipsius Christi contumeliam, & fidei Christianæ subuersionem & perniciosissima toti humano generi profudit. Siquis alias Arianorum hypotheses requirat, legat eorum sermonem qui extat apud Augustum Tom.6.
main_text.head: CAP. L. Audiani qui fuerint, & quod eorum dogma.

p.i: AUdianos quos appellant, (& Epiphanius schismaticos non hæreticos vult videri) alij vocant Anthropomorphitas, quoniam Deum sibi fingunt cogitatione carnali in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis: quod rusticitati eorum tribuit Epiphanius, parcens eis, ne dicantur hæretici. Eos autem separasse se dicit à [?]communione nostra culpando Episcopos di-uites [?], & Pascha cum Iudæis celebrando, quamuis sint qui eos in Ægypto Ecclesia Catholica communicare asseuerent. De Photinianis autem, quos [?]isto loco Epiphanius commemorat, iam superius sa-tis locutus sum.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "domminione" in the line "à domminione nostra" is unclear and marked [?]. "diuites" is also doubtful, as is "isto" at the start of the line "isto loco", where the first letter is damaged. The word "seperasse" is read as printed. The running head "Cap.50." is taken as the page number. The initial A is a woodcut letter and is joined to "Udianos" as "AUdianos". The catchword "Audianos" is at the foot right.
